newsitem.title: LEBANON: EU grants Beirut $48 mln to upgrade administration.
newsitem.headline: EU grants Beirut $48 mln to upgrade administration.

text.p: The European Union has approved a grant of 38 million ecus ($48 million) to the Lebanese government to help upgrade the public administration worn out in the 1975-90 civil war, a government official said on Wednesday.
The official of the administrative reform ministry told Reuters that the EU will pay the money to European firms to upgrade various government ministries and institutions in Lebanon.
The money would be spent on improving services and raising productivity in Lebanese public institutions, he added.

Outgoing Administrative Reform Minister Anwar al-Khalil said on Tuesday after meeting an EU delegation that the grant amounts to 40 percent of the total cost of upgrading the Lebanese administrative system, which he had put at $106 million.
Lebanon has launched a programme to rehabilitate its public administrative system in November 1995 with a $20 million loan from the World Bank.
The Kuwait-based Arab Development Fund granted Lebanon a $20-million soft loan in February for the same purpose.
